newsitem.title: USA: KCBT wheat ends higher, extends gains in late hike.
newsitem.headline: KCBT wheat ends higher, extends gains in late hike.

text.p: KCBT hard red winter wheat futures ended higher, extending earlier gains in a late surge tied to commission-related buying, traders said.
"We had market-on-close buying by Prudential and Linnco (LFG)," a KCBT trader said.
Traders said the late buying may have been tied to a report that India will need to import as much as five million tonnes of wheat in 1997-98.
KCBT wheat was bolstered early by concerns over possible winterkill damage to the wheat from cold temperatures expected later this week in the U.S. Plains.

"People continued to position themselves ahead of the big freeze," said one trader who appeared skeptical over potential winterkill damage to the crop. "You've got to realize that the crop is dormant and winterkill usually accounts for the least amount of crop damage."
KCBT wheat closed one to eight cents per bushel higher, with March up eight cents at $4.14, its highest close since Dec. 19. July gained three cents to close at $3.55.

Featured players included Benson-Quinn, which bought 1.5 million March bushels, and ADM's Smoot Grain, which sold one million March. FIMAT sold 1.3 million March. Farmland bought 800,000 March, traders said.
